title: When generating sprite animations, for example a building getting destroyed. How do you keep the parts of the building from going offscreen? That messes up the animation.
author: FutureLynx_
selftext: Thats the question. I have my building destroyed but parts of it go to the edges of the sprite and doesn't look okay. How do you prevent or fix this? Any work around?

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: Avoid game assets all together better to do it 100% procedural with code and math! 🔥

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: Ahh interesting but my game is 2d, so it needs sprites man. Or am i missing something? It seems procedural works better for 3d meshes. Right?

replies.author: Disastrous-Round-150
replies.body:
Nah... Both for 2d and 3d. 

This game of mine is 100% procedural, NEON RIFT

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YmWy6Hxd15c&t=17s](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YmWy6Hxd15c&t=17s)

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: Though for a 2d game like red alert 2 with sprite animations? That wont work? Thats more for 3d?

replies.author: Professor_Snipe
replies.body: You can always make the building consist of parts, or cut it up somehow along bricks (Claude will handle this well after a few iterations in my experience) and then use the engine to animate the collapse, aye?

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: the problem is that a building collapsing or getting destroyed always sends parts of it off the sprite. So the sprite animation is useless.

replies.author: Professor_Snipe
replies.body: So don't do sprite animation at all, just cut it up and collapse its parts engine-side?

comments.author: Internal-Capital7471
comments.body: Big smoke/fire animation and suddenly the parts are not there
